points.title: 童年启蒙
points.description: 乔布斯1955年出生于旧金山，被保罗和克拉拉·乔布斯收养。在山景城长大，对电子技术展现出早期兴趣。他经常与邻居工程师史蒂芬·沃兹尼亚克一起在车库里工作，这为他后来的创业奠定了基础。乔布斯就读于山景城的霍姆斯特德高中，并在那里结识了苹果公司的另一位重要人物史蒂夫·沃兹尼亚克。这段时期培养了他对简洁设计和卓越品质的追求，以及对传统教育体系的质疑态度。
points.descriptionEn: Born in San Francisco in 1955, Jobs was adopted by Paul and Clara Jobs. Raised in Mountain View, he showed an early interest in electronics. He frequently worked with neighbor engineer Steve Wozniak in garages, laying the foundation for his future entrepreneurship. Jobs attended Homestead High School in Mountain View, where he met another key figure at Apple, Steve Wozniak. This period cultivated his pursuit of simplicity, excellence in design, and skepticism toward traditional education.

points.title: 大学探索
points.description: 乔布斯进入里德学院学习，但仅六个月后便退学。尽管退学，他仍继续旁听课程，尤其是书法课，这对他后来对字体设计的重视产生了深远影响。这段时期他靠捡可乐罐和乞讨为生，同时探索东方哲学，特别是禅宗佛教，这塑造了他极简主义的设计哲学和对直觉的重视。1974年，乔布斯前往印度寻求精神启蒙，这段经历进一步深化了他对简约和专注的追求。
points.descriptionEn: Jobs attended Reed College but dropped out after six months. Despite leaving, he continued to audit classes, particularly a calligraphy course that profoundly influenced his later emphasis on typography. During this time, he supported himself by collecting Coke cans and begging while exploring Eastern philosophies, especially Zen Buddhism, which shaped his minimalist design philosophy and emphasis on intuition. In 1974, Jobs traveled to India seeking spiritual enlightenment, further deepening his pursuit of simplicity and focus.

points.place: 加利福尼亚州库比蒂诺
points.title: 苹果创立
points.description: 1976年4月1日，乔布斯与沃兹尼亚克在乔布斯家的车库里创立了苹果公司。他们推出了Apple I和Apple II计算机，后者取得了巨大成功，使苹果成为个人电脑领域的先驱。1980年，苹果公司上市，创造了当时历史上最大的IPO。1983年，乔布斯招募了百事可乐高管约翰·斯卡利担任苹果CEO，并留下名言'你是想一辈子卖糖水，还是想改变世界？'。然而，由于与斯卡利的战略分歧，1985年乔布斯被迫离开了自己创立的公司，这成为他人生中的一个重大挫折。
points.descriptionEn: On April 1, 1976, Jobs and Wozniak founded Apple Computer in Jobs' garage. They launched the Apple I and Apple II computers, with the latter becoming a massive success, making Apple a pioneer in the personal computer industry. In 1980, Apple went public, creating the largest IPO in history at that time. In 1983, Jobs recruited Pepsi executive John Sculley as Apple's CEO, famously asking, 'Do you want to sell sugar water for the rest of your life, or do you want to change the world?' However, due to strategic disagreements with Sculley, Jobs was forced to leave the company he founded in 1985, becoming a major setback in his life.

points.place: 加利福尼亚州帕洛阿尔托
points.title: NeXT时代
points.description: 离开苹果后，乔布斯创立了NeXT公司，专注于高端工作站市场，并收购了电脑动画部门，后来发展为皮克斯动画工作室。NeXT的技术创新，包括NeXTSTEP操作系统，为后来的苹果产品奠定了基础。尽管NeXT在商业上并不成功，但其技术理念影响了整个计算机行业。同时，乔布斯从皮克斯的成功中获得了商业经验，并重新发现了自己的创业激情。这段时间虽然远离了苹果的核心业务，但乔布斯仍在关注科技发展，并积累了宝贵的经验和人脉，为他重返苹果埋下了伏笔。
points.descriptionEn: After leaving Apple, Jobs founded NeXT, focusing on the high-end workstation market, and acquired a computer graphics division that later became Pixar Animation Studios. NeXT's technological innovations, including the NeXTSTEP operating system, laid the foundation for future Apple products. Although NeXT was not commercially successful, its technological concepts influenced the entire computer industry. Meanwhile, Jobs gained business experience from Pixar's success and rediscovered his entrepreneurial passion. During this period, though away from Apple's core business, Jobs continued to follow tech developments and accumulated valuable experience and connections, setting the stage for his return to Apple.

points.place: 加利福尼亚州库比蒂诺
points.title: 苹果复兴
points.description: 1997年，苹果收购NeXT，乔布斯以顾问身份重返苹果，随后成为临时CEO。他带领苹果推出了iMac、iPod、iPhone和iPad等一系列革命性产品，将苹果从濒临破产的边缘转变为全球最有价值的公司之一。乔布斯以其对产品设计的极致追求和对用户体验的重视，重新定义了多个科技行业。他建立了苹果独特的零售店模式，创造了全球最大的零售网络之一。2005年，乔布斯被诊断出胰腺癌，但他继续领导苹果直到2011年8月辞职。2011年10月5日，乔布斯因胰腺癌去世，享年56岁，留下了一个科技帝国和深远的文化影响。
points.descriptionEn: In 1997, Apple acquired NeXT, and Jobs returned to Apple as an advisor before becoming interim CEO. He led Apple to launch revolutionary products including the iMac, iPod, iPhone, and iPad, transforming the company from near-bankruptcy to one of the world's most valuable. With his extreme pursuit of product design and emphasis on user experience, Jobs redefined multiple tech industries. He established Apple's unique retail store model, creating one of the world's largest retail networks. In 2005, Jobs was diagnosed with pancreatic cancer but continued leading Apple until his resignation in August 2011. On October 5, 2011, Jobs died of pancreatic cancer at age 56, leaving behind a tech empire and profound cultural impact.

points.place: 加利福尼亚州帕洛阿尔托
points.title: 抗癌历程
points.description: 2004年，乔布斯被诊断出患有胰腺神经内分泌肿瘤，这是一种相对罕见的胰腺癌。他最初尝试通过特殊饮食疗法治疗，直到2009年才接受手术。2009年4月，乔布斯接受了肝脏移植手术，这是他对抗癌症的重要一步。2011年，他的健康状况进一步恶化，导致他多次请假并最终辞去苹果CEO职务。尽管面临健康挑战，乔布斯在生命的最后几年仍积极参与产品决策，特别是iPhone 4S和iPad 2的开发。他的抗癌历程展现了他面对死亡时的勇气和对工作的执着，也成为他人生故事中不可忽视的一部分。
points.descriptionEn: In 2004, Jobs was diagnosed with pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor, a rare form of pancreatic cancer. Initially, he tried treating it with special dietary therapies before undergoing surgery in 2009. In April 2009, Jobs received a liver transplant, a significant step in his cancer battle. By 2011, his health further deteriorated, leading to multiple medical leaves and ultimately his resignation as Apple CEO. Despite health challenges, Jobs remained actively involved in product decisions in his final years, particularly for the iPhone 4S and iPad 2. His cancer battle demonstrated his courage in facing death and dedication to work, becoming an integral part of his life story.

supporter.zh: 乔布斯被视为创新天才和设计大师，他重新定义了个人电脑、音乐、手机和动画电影等多个行业。他的产品理念——将技术与人文艺术完美结合——改变了人们与技术互动的方式。乔布斯对细节的极致追求和对用户体验的重视，创造了苹果独特的品牌价值和文化影响力。他证明了创新和设计可以成为商业成功的核心驱动力，激励了一代创业者追求卓越而非平庸。乔布斯的遗产不仅体现在苹果公司的市值上，更在于他改变了世界数十亿人的生活方式。
supporter.en: Jobs is regarded as an innovative genius and design master who redefined multiple industries including personal computers, music, mobile phones, and animated films. His product philosophy—perfectly combining technology with humanities and arts—transformed how people interact with technology. Jobs' extreme pursuit of detail and emphasis on user experience created Apple's unique brand value and cultural influence. He demonstrated that innovation and design could be core drivers of business success, inspiring a generation of entrepreneurs to pursue excellence rather than mediocrity. Jobs' legacy is not only reflected in Apple's market value but in how he changed the lifestyles of billions worldwide.

critic.zh: 乔布斯也面临诸多批评，包括他的管理风格被描述为专横和情绪化，对员工要求苛刻。他否认自己是亲生父亲，直到DNA测试才被迫承认。在商业决策上，乔布斯曾拒绝为苹果产品添加Flash支持，被批评为限制用户选择；他拒绝慈善捐赠，直到晚年才成立慈善基金会；他的封闭生态系统策略也被批评为反竞争。此外，乔布斯的产品发布会风格被一些人视为过度营销和自我炒作。这些批评反映了乔布斯性格中的矛盾性：追求极致创新的同时，也展现出人性中的弱点和道德争议。
critic.en: Jobs also faced significant criticism, including his management style described as autocratic and emotional, with demanding expectations of employees. He denied being the biological father of his daughter until DNA tests forced acknowledgment. In business decisions, Jobs' refusal to add Flash support to Apple products was criticized as limiting user choice; he avoided charitable donations until late in life when he established a foundation; his closed ecosystem strategy was also criticized as anti-competitive. Additionally, Jobs' product launch style was seen by some as excessive marketing and self-promotion. These criticisms reflect the contradictions in Jobs' character: while pursuing extreme innovation, he also exhibited human weaknesses and moral controversies.

objective.zh: 在历史和流行文化中，乔布斯已成为科技创新和创业精神的象征。他的'现实扭曲力场'、黑色高领衫和牛仔裤的形象，以及富有感染力的产品发布会，使他成为全球最具辨识度的商业领袖之一。乔布斯的故事被多次改编成电影、书籍和纪录片，成为创业神话的典型代表。然而，学术界也试图超越神话，探讨乔布斯成功背后的复杂因素，包括他对设计美学的执着、对用户体验的重视，以及将技术民主化的愿景。乔布斯既不是完美的圣人，也不是单纯的商业奇才，而是一个充满矛盾和复杂性的历史人物，他的遗产将继续影响科技和商业的未来发展。
objective.en: In history and popular culture, Jobs has become a symbol of technological innovation and entrepreneurial spirit. His 'reality distortion field,' image of black turtlenecks and jeans, and charismatic product launches made him one of the most recognizable business leaders globally. Jobs' story has been adapted into films, books, and documentaries, becoming a quintessential example of startup mythology. Academically, however, efforts have been made to move beyond the myth, exploring the complex factors behind Jobs' success, including his obsession with design aesthetics, emphasis on user experience, and vision to democratize technology. Jobs was neither a perfect saint nor merely a business prodigy, but a complex historical figure full of contradictions, whose legacy will continue to influence the future of technology and business.

others.zh: 他拥有一种非凡的能力，能够理解人类心理学，并将这种理解融入到他创造的产品中。他不是简单地满足需求，而是创造需求。
others.en: He had an extraordinary ability to understand human psychology and incorporate that understanding into the products he created. He didn't just satisfy needs, he created them.
